title: Submodules: a repository pinned inside another repository
summary: Add a shared library as a submodule, understand that the parent stores a commit sha rather than files, and survive the detached-HEAD trap that catches everyone the first time.
mental_model: The parent repository stores one thing per submodule: the exact commit sha it wants. The submodule's files are not in the parent's history at all. That pin is the whole feature — and the whole difficulty.
danger: Committing inside a submodule while it is on a detached HEAD makes commits that no branch points at. Push fails, and the work is reachable only through the reflog.

steps.title: Add the library as a submodule
steps.why: `submodule add` clones it into a subdirectory and stages two things: a `.gitmodules` file describing where it came from, and a special index entry recording which commit is pinned.

steps.title: See what the parent actually stores
steps.why: `ls-files -s` shows mode 160000 — a gitlink. Not a file, not a tree: a pointer to a commit in another repository. The library's source code is not in this repository at all.

verify.label: the parent stores a gitlink, not files

steps.title: Clone the parent and find an empty directory
steps.why: A plain clone creates the submodule directory and leaves it empty. This is the single most reported submodule problem, and it is intended behaviour — the pin is there, the content is not fetched.
steps.expect: An empty directory, and a status line prefixed with - meaning uninitialised. (The clone uses an absolute path: a relative submodule URL in .gitmodules is resolved against the superproject's remote URL, so cloning from '.' would resolve it wrongly.)

steps.title: Initialise and fetch the pinned commit
steps.why: `--init --recursive` reads .gitmodules, clones each submodule, and checks out exactly the pinned sha. `git clone --recurse-submodules` does it in one step at clone time.
steps.expect: The library's files appear, at the pinned commit.

verify.label: the submodule content is present in the clone

steps.title: Look inside — you are detached
steps.why: A submodule is checked out at a commit, not a branch, because the parent pins a sha. Committing here creates work no branch points at. Always `git switch main` inside a submodule before editing.
steps.expect: HEAD detached at the pinned commit.

steps.title: Update the library and move the pin
steps.why: Two commits are needed: one in the submodule, one in the parent recording the new sha. Forgetting the second is why colleagues report 'it works for you but not for me'.
commands: git commit -q -m "Bump sensor library to include salinity"
steps.expect: The parent's status shows the submodule as modified — meaning its pin changed.

verify.label: the parent recorded the new pin
verify.hint: after updating the submodule, git add the submodule path in the parent

steps.title: Check every submodule at once
steps.why: `submodule status` in the parent, and `--recurse-submodules` on fetch and push, are how you avoid the classic failure: pushing a parent that pins a commit nobody else can fetch.

verify.label: submodule.recurse is on, so pull and checkout keep submodules in step
the parent pins the library by commit sha
.gitmodules records where the submodule comes from
the pin was moved forward in its own parent commit
verify.hint: updating a submodule always takes two commits

verify.label: the working tree has the updated library

pitfalls: A fresh clone leaves submodule directories empty. Use `git clone --recurse-submodules`, or run `git submodule update --init --recursive` immediately after.
Submodules check out detached. `git switch main` inside one before committing, or your commits belong to no branch.
Push the submodule BEFORE pushing the parent. Otherwise the parent pins a commit nobody else can fetch, and every colleague's checkout fails.
`git submodule update` without `--merge` or `--rebase` throws away local commits in the submodule by resetting to the pinned sha.
For internal code you control, a monorepo or a package registry is usually less painful than submodules.
cheatsheet: vendor a repository at a path
clone with content, not empty directories
which sha each submodule is pinned to
run a command in every submodule
